question: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$, if $\text{adj}(A)=A$, what are the possible values of $a, b, c, d$ when $ad-bc \ne 0$?
explanation:
$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$
So:
$a = d$, $b = -b$, $c=-c$, $d=a$
So $b = 0$, $c = 0$, $a = d$
So $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & a \end{bmatrix}$
$ad - bc = a^2 \ne 0 \implies a \ne 0$
Thus, $A$ is a nonzero multiple of the identity matrix.

options.A: $a=d=0$, $b$ and $c$ can be any non-zero real numbers
